trend.title: CMBS Delinquencies Climb to 8.02% in September as Multifamily Leads Rate Increase
trend.summary: Trepp's monthly CMBS surveillance found that the volume of loans more than 30 days delinquent rose $1.23 billion, or 2.6%, in September 2026 to $48.65 billion, pushing the overall delinquency rate to 8.02% of the $606.58 billion universe tracked. The multifamily sector's delinquency rate rose 35 basis points in September, the largest increase of any property type tracked, continuing to drive the broader increase in late payments across the CMBS market.
trend.significance: Lenders, special servicers, and borrowers' counsel should treat the continued climb in delinquencies as a leading indicator of more contested foreclosure and workout litigation across property types, not just the office sector that has dominated distress headlines this year. A rising multifamily delinquency rate in particular signals that loan-default litigation risk, long concentrated in office, is broadening into other asset classes.
